docs/guide/audio.md:62:*Agents:* `set_audio` (`clips`, `patch`) changes any of these properties on one or more clips. Its patch keys are `volume`, `muted`, `fade_in`, `fade_out`, `fade_in_shape`, `fade_out_shape`, `duck`, `mono`, `keep_pitch`, `pan`, `compressor`, `noise_reduction` and `limiter`. Setting `duck`, `compressor` or `limiter` to null turns it off. `get_project` reads them back.
docs/guide/audio.md:81:You can animate a clip's sound with actions. While an action is selected, the Volume row, Mute and the fade lengths write that action's end state, and so do Pan, Mix to mono, Channels, the EQ, Hum, Voice Isolation's Amount, Noise Reduction, the Gate, the Leveller, the De-esser, the Compressor and the Limiter. Numbers move smoothly across the action's span: a pan sweeps from one side to the other, an EQ band's gain rises, a compressor's threshold drifts, the isolated voice fades in. Switches change at the action's end, with no glide: Mix to mono, Channels, EQ Bypass, a pass filter's slope, Hum's mains and harmonics, the Leveller's Response, and turning a section or an EQ slot on or off. Unticking a section or an EQ slot with an action selected turns it off at the action's end. What you hear in the preview is what an export writes.
docs/guide/audio.md:85:Ducking, Keep pitch, the fade shapes and the voice effect can't be animated, and neither can a nest clip's Mix to mono. They always change the clip's own settings, even with an action selected.
docs/guide/audio.md:102:- **Loudness** (the default) sets each clip's volume so its integrated loudness (BS.1770, as the export plays it) reaches the target, **−16 LUFS** unless you choose another. Every clip goes to the same target, so this is how you match clips. A clip whose true peak would pass **−1 dBTP** at that volume gets its **Limiter** turned on at −1 dBTP in the same step, and its volume is the one that reaches the target through the limiter; a clip that already has a limiter keeps it, with its ceiling lowered to −1 dBTP if it was higher. A clip that would need more than 3200 % stops there and lands quieter than the target. A volume can go down as well as up. A mono clip is measured as the export plays it, on both channels, which reads 3 dB louder than the file on its own. A quiet desktop USB microphone recording, for example, measures −41.7 LUFS with peaks at −18.5 dBTP; one press takes it to −16 LUFS with the limiter holding −1 dBTP.
docs/guide/audio.md:105:- **It measures the clip, not the mix.** The level is read from the clip's cached waveform (Peak) or loudness analysis (Loudness) over the part of the file that actually plays. The clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and solo, and its track's volume and pan, don't affect the reading. Mix to mono and pan on a stereo clip do count in Loudness mode.
docs/guide/audio.md:131:Everything else (hum removal, the channel choice, pan, mono, fades, ducking, Mute, Keep pitch, the EQ's other parts) is left alone. Like Normalize, it writes the clip's base settings even inside an action. Nothing it chooses depends on what it wrote, so pressing it again changes nothing, and so does Normalize at the same target afterwards. On a desktop USB microphone recording (−41.6 LUFS, its pauses 20 dB under the voice) it turns on isolation, a gate at −6 dB and a compressor at −41 dBFS with 10 dB of makeup, leaves the leveller off (its speech's range is 4.6 LU), and the export lands at −16.0 LUFS with peaks at −1.0 dBTP and the pauses about 28 dB quieter than with Normalize alone.
docs/guide/audio.md:279:Use Left Only or Right Only for a microphone recorded onto one channel of a stereo file: the voice then plays from both speakers at its own level, and the Volume section's Loudness read-out counts it that way. The choice comes right after voice isolation, before the EQ and the mono fold. A mono file has only one channel, so the choice has no effect on it.

docs/guide/audio.md:435:The section summary reads "centre", "mono" or the pan position. Reset sets the pan back to centre and turns mono off.
docs/guide/audio.md:438:- **Pan has no effect on a clip whose source is mono.**
docs/guide/audio.md:439:- **Turn on Mix to mono as well to get a true pan.** The mono fold happens before the pan, so both channels then carry the same signal and Pan places that one signal anywhere from left to right.
docs/guide/audio.md:440:- **Mix to mono has no effect on a one-channel source.**
docs/guide/audio.md:442:*Agents:* `set_audio` with `pan` from −1 to 1 and `mono`.
docs/guide/audio.md:542:- **Pan is a balance, like a clip's pan.** It keeps the overall loudness steady as it moves, and it has no effect on a mono source.
docs/guide/audio.md:543:- **Nests hear their tracks.** A clip inside a nest plays through its own track inside the nest and through the track the nest clip sits on. Nesting a selection from one track keeps its sound: the nest's copy of that track starts at 0 dB and centre, because the track the nest clip lands on still applies. Clips from the selection's other tracks keep their own track's volume and pan inside the nest, and also get the destination track's. Un-nesting puts the clips back on the timeline's tracks without the nest's track settings. If a nest clip has **Mix to mono** on, pans of the tracks inside it no longer apply.

app_defects.title: File menu item reads New Recording… while choosing it stops the start in progress
app_defects.evidence: AppDelegate.swift:196 sets the title from ScreenRecorder.shared.isRecording, which is false during the panel's display lookup because the recorder is still idle. AppDelegate+Recording.swift newRecording routes panel phase .starting to panel.stopRecording(), and RecorderPanelController+Recording.swift:113 then calls abandonStart. So an item labelled New Recording… (⌥⌘N) abandons the recording. The panel's button is disabled in .starting (RecorderPanelController+Pause.swift:150-151), so this mislabelled item is the panel's only way to stop at that point.
